finding.title: Global curve-flattening change alters output for all rendering
finding.message: The scroll-surface patch rewrites the shared Bezier flattening in fill.go (QuadBezierF and CubeBezierF). Every path fill and stroke in rasterx goes through it, so output changes for all rendering, not just scrolling surfaces. Coordinates are now flattened relative to the control-hull minimum, and float32 truncation toward zero is applied to those relative values instead of absolute ones. For curves that cross zero this can move individual edge samples by one fixed unit compared with the old output, which can shift antialiasing and break existing golden-image tests. The curve tests only check translation invariance, not parity with the previous output.
finding.suggestion: Either confirm and document that the new flattening is acceptable for all renderers by running the existing golden and raster tests, or confine the translation-stable flattening to the scroll-verification path. Add a regression test that compares the new flattening against the old one for non-translated curves.
